q: What is the chemical symbol for Gold?
exp: Gold's chemical symbol is Au, from the Latin word 'Aurum'.
ai_exp:
Chemical Symbol Analysis:

• Go = Not a valid symbol ✗
• Gd = Gadolinium ✗
• Au = Gold (from Latin 'Aurum') ✓
• Ag = Silver (from Latin 'Argentum') ✗

Gold's symbol comes from its Latin name:
Aurum → Au

Option A: Invalid symbol ✗
Option B: Different element (Gadolinium) ✗
Option C: Gold ✓ Correct!
Option D: Different element (Silver) ✗

The correct answer is C) Au.

q: The atomic number of an element is determined by the number of:
exp: Atomic number = number of protons in the nucleus.
ai_exp:
Atomic Structure Analysis:

• Atomic number (Z) = Number of PROTONS
• Mass number (A) = Protons + Neutrons
• Electrons = Protons (in neutral atom)

Option A (Neutrons): Determines isotopes ✗
Option B (Protons): Determines atomic number ✓ Correct!
Option C (Electrons): Equals protons in neutral atoms ✗
Option D (Nucleons): Total protons + neutrons = mass number ✗

The correct answer is B) Protons.

q: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
exp: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.
ai_exp:
Atmospheric Composition:

• Nitrogen (N₂) = 78% ← Most abundant
• Oxygen (O₂) = 21%
• Carbon Dioxide (CO₂) = 0.04%
• Others (Argon, etc.) = 1%

Option A (Oxygen): 21%, second most ✗
Option B (CO₂): Only 0.04% ✗
Option C (Nitrogen): 78%, most abundant ✓ Correct!
Option D (Hydrogen): Trace amounts ✗

The correct answer is C) Nitrogen.

q: The pH of pure water at 25°C is:
exp: Pure water is neutral with a pH of 7.
ai_exp:
pH Scale Analysis:

• pH 0-6: Acidic
• pH 7: Neutral
• pH 8-14: Basic/Alkaline

Pure water at 25°C:
• [H⁺] = [OH⁻]
• Perfectly neutral
• pH = 7

Option A (0): Strongly acidic ✗
Option B (5): Acidic ✗
Option C (7): Neutral ✓ Correct!
Option D (14): Strongly basic ✗

The correct answer is C) 7.

q: Which of the following is a noble gas?
exp: Argon is a noble gas in Group 18 of the periodic table.
ai_exp:
Noble Gases (Group 18):
• Helium (He)
• Neon (Ne)
• Argon (Ar) ← This one!
• Krypton (Kr)
• Xenon (Xe)
• Radon (Rn)

Noble gases are unreactive due to full outer electron shells.

Option A (Oxygen): Group 16 ✗
Option B (Nitrogen): Group 15 ✗
Option C (Argon): Group 18 - Noble gas ✓ Correct!
Option D (Chlorine): Group 17 - Halogen ✗

The correct answer is C) Argon.

q: The chemical formula for water is:
exp: Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom: H₂O.
ai_exp:
Chemical Formula Analysis:

• CO₂ = Carbon dioxide (1 carbon + 2 oxygen) ✗
• H₂O = Water (2 hydrogen + 1 oxygen) ✓
• O₂ = Oxygen gas (2 oxygen atoms) ✗
• NaCl = Sodium chloride (salt) ✗

Water formula:
• H₂O = 2 hydrogen atoms + 1 oxygen atom

Option A: Carbon dioxide ✗
Option B: Water ✓ Correct!
Option C: Oxygen gas ✗
Option D: Table salt ✗

The correct answer is B) H₂O.

q: Which bond type involves the sharing of electrons?
exp: Covalent bonds form when atoms share electron pairs.
ai_exp:
Chemical Bond Analysis:

• Ionic bond: Transfer of electrons (metal + non-metal) ✗
• Covalent bond: SHARING of electrons (non-metal + non-metal) ✓
• Metallic bond: Sea of delocalized electrons ✗
• Hydrogen bond: Weak intermolecular force ✗

Covalent bond examples:
• H₂O, CO₂, CH₄

Option A: Electron transfer ✗
Option B: Electron sharing ✓ Correct!
Option C: Electron sea ✗
Option D: Weak attraction ✗

The correct answer is B) Covalent bond.

q: The molar mass of oxygen gas (O₂) is approximately:
exp: O₂ has two oxygen atoms (16 × 2 = 32 g/mol).
ai_exp:
Molar Mass Calculation:

• Atomic mass of O = 16 g/mol
• O₂ = 2 oxygen atoms
• Molar mass of O₂ = 2 × 16 = 32 g/mol

Option A (16): Mass of ONE oxygen atom ✗
Option B (32): 2 × 16 = 32 ✓ Correct!
Option C (8): Half of oxygen atom ✗
Option D (64): 4 oxygen atoms ✗

The correct answer is B) 32 g/mol.

q: Which indicator turns red in acidic solution?
exp: Methyl orange turns red in acidic solutions.
ai_exp:
Indicator Color Analysis:

• Litmus: Red in acid, Blue in base ✗
• Phenolphthalein: Colorless in acid, Pink in base ✗
• Methyl orange: RED in acid, Yellow in base ✓
• Universal: Multiple colors ✗

Methyl orange specifically turns RED in acid.

Option A: Also red in acid, but the specific one asked ✓ (but methyl orange is the classic answer)
Option B: Colorless in acid ✗
Option C: Red in acid ✓ Correct!
Option D: Shows different colors ✗

The correct answer is C) Methyl orange.

q: The chemical symbol for Sodium is:
exp: Sodium's chemical symbol is Na, from the Latin 'Natrium'.
ai_exp:
Chemical Symbol Analysis:

• S = Sulfur ✗
• So = Invalid symbol ✗
• Na = Sodium (from Latin 'Natrium') ✓
• K = Potassium (from Latin 'Kalium') ✗

Sodium → Na (Latin: Natrium)

Option A: Sulfur ✗
Option B: Invalid ✗
Option C: Sodium ✓ Correct!
Option D: Potassium ✗

The correct answer is C) Na.
